feedback.finish: Sucking in air through your mouth and nose is not enough to get it all the way to the lungs. We have to rely on some special muscles instead!

atoms.b: When we inhale, the ((++diaphragm heart)) moves downwards and the ribs move outwards as the muscles contract.
This means that the space inside your chest gets ((++bigger smaller)) and there is a change in air pressure. This causes ((++air helium)) to be pulled into the lungs.

The ((++opposite same_thing)) happens when we exhale. Our muscles relax, so the diaphragm moves ((++upwards diagonally)) and the ribs come back in. Therefore, the chest cavity gets smaller, and air is squeezed out.

text: Try it for yourself! Place a hand on your chest and take some deep breaths to feel your chest getting bigger and smaller.

instruction.text: Which body parts make the chest move when we inhale and exhale?
